questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with a lot of international students and I wanted to go to a country within the EU. Furthermore, I did not want to go somewhere where school would be very time demanding. Apart from that, I have always liked Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. You need to find the information yourself on the website of the university regarding courses and so on. However, the most crucial thing are sent to you via e-mail, which helps.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was the responsible person, Massimo, at the University of Milan. He was quite helpful and answered my questions quickly. 
However, there was not really any guidance on how to navigate the school or websites of the school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing via Idealista, but please be aware of scams. We found it via an agency which made a rental contract.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very expensive, especially if you want to live in the center of Milan. However, the housing for students is cheap (around 2000 DKK per month). You get the email to access student housing late (around June/July). Almost everyone that I know, that wanted to stay at student accommodation got one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the beginning, you can 'shop courses' and try different courses. It is easy to register them. You receive an email with the registration process. I tried one course that I did not end up taking. It is very chill and relax and everyone got the courses they wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a guide, which was sent to us via e-mail. You can always ask the teachers.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to make a good schedule. I was off on Mondays which was very nice, and if you have breaks between classes that is nice, because you can always grab a coffee with your classmates

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the courses were easier than at my home university. There was almost no preparation before class. However, some classes are harder and more demanding than others, but never as demanding as at Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In some classes, your grades depended on your contribution during class. Furthermore, we did not do group work and a lot of classes were just listening. The classes I took were only seminars and not big lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Competition Law and economics
2) Theory and practice of international tax law
3) Smart cities, Artificial intelligence and digital transformation law
4) International, European environmental law 
5) Roman law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Competition law and economic and theory and practice of international law were the most useful ones and the ones were I learned the most. If you want a very easy exam and no homework, the smart cities class is a good choice. I would not recommend the environmental law class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent can be quite expensive. Furthermore, the general cost of living (restaurant and so on) is cheaper than in Copenhagen, but Milan is probably the most expensive part of Italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ESN did a lot of activities and every Tuesday night there is a gypsy bar where you meet a lot of international students. I would really recommend to engage in those activities. you meet a lot of amazing people and it is very interesting to meet people from other cultures.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not really engage in the activities hosted by the host university and to be honest, I do not know whether they hosted any for international students. It was more via the ESN community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Engage in the ESN activities - especially in the beginning. People are very open.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do trips around Italy with Flixbus. You can see Verona, Florence, Venice or Bologna

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. However, there was a language barrier and sometimes Milanese can be a bit rude if you do not speak Italian.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialize that much with Italian students, but my experience is that once you talk to them, they are pretty open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are a bit more relaxed here and sometimes things are not that organized.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved their apperitivo concept and their sense of style.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) They tell you that exams are in January. That is not necessarily true - I had all mine in December before Christmas. Each course has four rounds of exam dates, one in December, two in January and one in February. You can choose which ever you prefer. So, you do not need accommodation until January (that was at least the case for law - regarding Medicine it was different)
- Law courses first start around late September (mine started around 20th of September) 
- Don't stress regarding course registration and exam registration - you will receive intructions.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to know Milan very well, which is very nice. Furthermore, I met so many amazing people and I think it made me more open and able to talk to a lot of different people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning you have to get used to everything and the fact that all your routines are different, but as soon as school starts, everything feels normal.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
